{
  "verdict": "fix",
  "issues": [
    "Missing error response definitions (e.g., 400 Bad Request, 404 Not Found) in the endpoint contracts.",
    "Lack of a PATCH method for partial updates; PUT requires full resource replacement which is inefficient for simple status changes.",
    "The custom JSON schema uses informal type definitions (e.g., 'enum: ...') and lacks field-level validation rules (required vs. optional fields, string constraints).",
    "GET /tasks returns an unbounded array (Task[]), risking performance and memory issues as data grows, with no pagination or limit mechanism defined.",
    "Reinventing a custom JSON schema instead of using OpenAPI/Swagger forfeits standard tooling, automated client generation, and interactive documentation."
  ],
  "suggestions": [
    "Add standard error response structures and define 4xx/5xx status codes for each endpoint to handle validation and not-found scenarios.",
    "Introduce a PATCH /tasks/{id} endpoint for partial updates, or explicitly document that PUT requires the complete resource payload.",
    "Refine the resource schema to explicitly mark required fields (e.g., title) and define strict data types, formats, and constraints.",
    "Implement basic pagination (e.g., limit and offset query parameters) or a hard cap on the GET /tasks collection endpoint.",
    "Adopt the OpenAPI 3.0 specification instead of a custom JSON format to leverage existing ecosystem tools and standard documentation."
  ]
}
